claim.quote: We present results from the tests of the first fabricated Oscura prototype sensors, evaluate their performance in the context of the established constraints and estimate the Oscura instrumental background based on these results.

name: Skipper-CCD Sensors for the Oscura Experiment: Requirements and Preliminary Tests
notes: Technology milestone, not a dark matter result: no Oscura physics result has been published.

summary.plain: The Oscura team made its first prototype sensors, tested them against the strict noise and background limits the experiment needs, and estimated how many false events the final detector would see from the sensors themselves.
summary.technical: Instrumental-background requirements for the Oscura skipper-CCDs (parameters of the sensors, 2-10 electron signal region, 0.01 dru radiation goal at SNOLAB depth 2070 m) and first tests of the prototype sensors made at a new foundry; the instrumental background is estimated from the measurements.

title: Skipper-CCD Sensors for the Oscura Experiment: Requirements and Preliminary Tests
why_it_matters: The paper states Oscura aims for less than one event in each electron bin in 2-10 electrons for the full 30 kg-year exposure, so the sensors' own backgrounds must be controlled.
